records.region: Alaska; Angle Creek–Takayofo Creek–King Salmon River corridor and Egegik receiving-estuary surroundings
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen opening and its northwest passage across mapped glacier/ice terrain into the Angle Creek channel network are not established as a mapped watercourse or hydraulic through-link.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The mapped route below the initial glaciated opening is Angle Creek, then Takayofo Creek, then King Salmon River. These named components and the King Salmon receiving-river corridor are supported locally. A completed representative name for the whole selection is withheld because the initial ice-to-channel passage is not established. Egegik River is a separate receiving-estuary context, not a selected whole-object name.
records.completion_scope: Four inspected original USGSTopo views establish the Angle Creek–Takayofo Creek–King Salmon River sequence and the mapped named-component joins through the lower estuarine terminal. The actual chosen opening crosses depicted glacier/ice terrain without a source-depicted watercourse establishing that initial through-link. The single primary status is material-pending, not a completed representative identity or naming-scope hold. The first acquisition timeout was resolved by the sole identical-URL retry; no new access stop remains.
records.supported_name_scope: The mapped route below the initial glaciated opening is Angle Creek, then Takayofo Creek, then King Salmon River. These named components and the King Salmon receiving-river corridor are supported locally. A completed representative name for the whole selection is withheld because the initial ice-to-channel passage is not established. Egegik River is a separate receiving-estuary context, not a selected whole-object name.

scope_limits: The glaciated initial passage remains a material evidence gap. Mapped ice, adjacent channels and modeled connectivity cannot establish a continuous surface or subglacial watercourse.
Angle Creek, Takayofo Creek and King Salmon River are distinct named components; neither King Salmon River nor Egegik River is accepted as a scalar name for every part.

The actual rendered terminal is in the lower King Salmon estuarine corridor upstream of the visible Egegik joining area. The modeled sea classification is not adopted as source evidence for an open-sea endpoint.

The selection is generalized and clips local river bends. Exact banks, braid choices, name-transition vertices, glacier margins, tides, perennial flow and present water conditions remain outside scope.
No selected through-lake or reservoir passage is established or required by the inspected corridor; adjacent lakes remain separate waterbodies.
Formal registry status and Korean name selection remain unverified.

records.material_pending_reason: The selected Buenos Aires coastal-plain system remains source-material pending. An independent provincial road-project report supplies historical context for lagoons, canals, sluices and separate estuarine/saltmarsh outlets, but its inspected maps do not establish the complete selected opening, connecting reaches and terminal. No whole-system name is assigned.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No supported whole-system name or selected component name. The credited sources establish regional mixed coastal drainage context, but do not establish every chosen reach and joining connection. No natural-river identity is forced onto possible drainage works.
records.completion_scope: One successful independent road-project original was read, with separately identified embedded source material. All19 selected parts are accounted for in seven component groups. Because actual selected connections remain unresolved, this is one material-pending finding rather than a completed naming-scope hold. The bounded pass ends without repeated source expansion.
records.supported_name_scope: No supported whole-system name or selected component name. The credited sources establish regional mixed coastal drainage context, but do not establish every chosen reach and joining connection. No natural-river identity is forced onto possible drainage works.

scope_limits: All19 selected geometry parts were reviewed for orientation, but geographic correspondence to a continuous source-supported water route remains incomplete.
The long straight reaches and reversals are properties of the supplied modeled path, not proof of a named canal or natural river.
Regional lagoon overflows, managed connections and estuarine/saltmarsh outlets cannot substitute for the chosen through-links.
Modeled length is not an official measured river length. Exact banks, present shorelines, hydraulic operation, legal registry status and Korean forms are unverified.
A lack of selected-route correspondence does not prove that a channel is absent or locally unnamed.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
